findings.description: [demoted to minor: no concrete failure scenario, so it cannot gate; reported as major by the reviewer] The inventory frame includes location alarm_mode, ownership and time_zone, but only device entries carry state_version. The latest-wins rule also applies only per device, and the Location entity in data-model.md has no version. If inventory A fails to commit, newer inventory B commits with a changed alarm mode, and A is resent after 10 seconds, the specified protocol provides no ordering value with which to reject A's older location fields. Device state remains current while the overview's stored location alarm mode can roll back, violating FR-001 and FR-006. Define ordering for location state as well, such as a durable location revision or inventory generation, and carry it through State and T018/T019. Include the failed-A, committed-B, retried-A case for location fields in the planned tests.
findings.title: Protect location state against older inventory retries

These remain active plan-resolution references, including citations from the revised Audit section, so implementers and reviewers receive contradictory scope instructions. Update PT-19 and G4 to the approved iteration-002 start while retaining iteration 004 for WORM shipping.
findings.title: Update the remaining audit-start decisions after DRIFT-001-04

summary: Completed risk-based inspection of the frozen planning, contract, schema and CI-workflow snapshot. Application implementation is absent, so this is not runtime assurance. Coverage included identity and enrollment boundaries, state freshness, retry ordering, event recovery, schema consistency, deployment bootstrap and verification planning. The controller's one declared governance command succeeded with exit code 0 and no timeout; no tests or builds were run by this reviewer. Two findings remain. The documented iteration-002 recovery-summary deferral and T004 workflow repairs were considered as existing planned work.
